profile.headline: Android Automotive at Google
profile.summary:
My passion is to make computers do useful things for people. This led to my first job at Silicon Graphics, where I learned OpenGL from some of the people who invented it. Then it drove me to work on the first MP3 players, the first smartphones, and the Tesla car interface, where I wrote the Autopilot visualization and subsequently directed their user interface (UI) engineering team.

We live in a world where software distinguishes a good product from a bad one. I love to create the amazing software that powers outstanding products.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Mountain View, California, United States · On-site

positions.title: Chief Executive Officer
positions.description:
vehicle.software is creating a new infotainment platform to redefine the in-car experience.

We are hiring engineers and designers, please reach out!

positions.title: Engineering
positions.description: After completing the initial few software releases for Model 3 customers, I decided to take a break and worked on some fun projects with friends.

positions.title: Software Engineering Manager
positions.description:
While directing Tesla's UI team, I drove the following major new software releases and feature updates for the in-car screens and the phone app:

* The 8.0 release introduced a new map interface, new map renderer and new media player.
* The Model 3 UI established an entirely new UI design, with our own highly efficient vector map renderer.
* The V3 Tesla Mobile app consolidated two disparate codebases into a single one, integrating Tesla Energy, Sales Promotions, and Service scheduling and alerts, in a fresh new UI design that works on Android and iOS.
* The Phone Key system allows walk-up unlock without needing to get your phone out of your pocket. My team made the phone-side software, created an automated hardware-in-loop test suite, and worked closely with Apple and Google to ensure that their Bluetooth LE test suites included Tesla's specific usage.
* Inspired directly by customer feedback, my team added countless other new features including Climate Keeper, Summon, and the Navigation UI.

positions.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: I wrote Tesla's Autopilot, Autopark and Parking Sensor visualizations first released in 7.0 in October, 2015, in partnership with designer Bas Ording. I also built the 2D graphics framework that renders Tesla's UI; it aggressively optimizes for fill rate to ensure excellent performance even on the Tegra 2 and Tegra 3 of the original Model S.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description: Palm acquired Iventor's assets. I developed and conceptualized multi-tasking user interfaces and system software for handheld devices. Based on this work we made patent applications 20090189915 (now granted, US Pat # 8004541), 20090210441. From discussions and mock-ups inspired by this work we made further patent applications: 20090300542, 20090293007.

positions.title: Technical Yahoo
positions.description: I work on making Yahoo's services accessible through home digital media devices, in addition to engineering Windows client software.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
CoSpeed make small boxes which go inside payphones and dial SBC/Verizon when the payphone needs collection or maintenance. I wrote the server side software which answers the call from the payphone, extracts all of the required data from the payphone (such as coin counts, alarm states, reason for calling, etc), updates the payphones firmware and table of call rates and logs everything into a database.

Over one hundred thousand units have been deployed to the field, and my software runs for months at a time without restart.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I started working for Customer Service Sales in the UK on small internal software tools. After a short time, I moved to Global Product Support (GPS) and worked on other, larger internal tools (ensuring service level agreements were met, etc).

At the end of 2002 I moved to engineering, where I worked on OpenOffice for IRIX, and on core IRIX desktop. I did a lot of the work porting the IRIX desktop to SGI's UltimateVision graphics platform (which shipped in the Onyx 4).
